meta.title: Visa Has Never Lent You a Dollar. It's Still Worth More Than Most Banks.
meta.hook: Visa and Mastercard have never lent you a single dollar. They still make billions off every swipe.
meta.description: Visa and Mastercard don't issue cards or extend credit — your bank does. The networks earn fees for routing transactions between the merchant's bank and your bank, collecting a small cut of nearly every card swipe rather than taking on lending risk. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Visa and Mastercard have never lent you a single dollar.

visual.visual_intent: A card being tapped on a payment terminal, close macro, warm retail light

scenes.narration: They don't issue your card, and they don't decide if you're approved. Your bank does that.

visual.visual_intent: A modern bank branch interior, clean daylight, wide shot

scenes.narration: Visa and Mastercard just run the network that routes the transaction between your bank and the merchant's bank.

visual.visual_intent: Glowing connected network lines between nodes, dark background, abstract data flow

scenes.narration: For that, they collect a small fee on nearly every transaction that crosses their rails.

visual.visual_intent: Small coins dropping one at a time in a steady rhythm, macro, dark background

overlays.text: A fraction of a cent × billions of swipes

scenes.narration: Multiply a fraction of a cent by billions of swipes a day, and the fee becomes the entire business.

visual.visual_intent: A world map with countless glowing transaction points pulsing across it, dark, cinematic

scenes.narration: The lending risk, whether you actually pay your bill, sits with the issuing bank, not with Visa or Mastercard.
